questions.prompt: What is wrong with moving guest n to ⌊n/2⌋?
questions.context: A hotel has rooms 1,2,3,… and every room is occupied. Guests and arrivals are indexed by positive integers.
options: It only fails because infinitely many rooms exist.
It is injective but not onto.
Every guest keeps the same room.
It creates collisions and can assign room 0.
hints: A valid reassignment must avoid collisions and reserve enough rooms for every arrival.

questions.prompt: Why can a countable union of countable sets be enumerated in this setting?
questions.context: A hotel has rooms 1,2,3,… and every room is occupied. Guests and arrivals are indexed by positive integers.
options: Every union contains only finitely many elements.
Every set must have exactly the same elements.
Index elements by a pair (set index, within-set index) and traverse diagonally, skipping repetitions.
List one infinite set completely before starting the next.
hints: A valid reassignment must avoid collisions and reserve enough rooms for every arrival.
